headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: aci can push CRM/email data into broad-network transformers workflows, while shared write/network capabilities create conflict and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can pass content through MCP/direct function calls, and transformers can read files/stdin and run browsers/subprocesses. If aci forwards untrusted CRM/email text into transformers, prompt-like instructions can be embedded in shared content. No explicit provenance or isolation is documented for either agent, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF aci forwards user-controlled email or CRM text into transformers inputs
IF transformers treats file or stdin content as instructions rather than inert data
mitigations: Add a strict content-delimiting wrapper before passing text between agents
Strip or neutralize instruction-like tokens from aci outputs
Require transformers to operate on a schema, not raw prose
Log and review any cross-agent prompt handoff for one day
requires-engineering: add provenance tags across the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data and has broad network egress; transformers can read files and also has broad egress. If they share a workspace or hand off files, sensitive data can leave the local boundary through either agent. The profiles do not show isolation or DPA controls, so uncertainty pushes this upward.
conditions: IF aci and transformers share a filesystem, workspace, or OAuth principal
IF either agent sends shared content to an external API or hub
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials for each agent
Disable network egress for one agent during sensitive runs
Move sensitive files out of any shared directory
Review outbound destinations for both agents before execution
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API actions, while transformers can execute shell, install packages, write files, and spawn subprocesses. If both operate on the same directory or mutable resource, concurrent writes and state corruption are realistic. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so the default overlap is dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path, git repo, or database
IF aci triggers API-side state changes while transformers edits local artifacts
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories and resource scopes
Run only one writer at a time for shared assets
Use file locks or a queue around mutable resources
Snapshot state before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and transformers can execute shell or browser workflows. If transformers consumes aci output as authoritative, a mistaken lead, email, or calendar action can cascade into external side effects. The pair lacks documented verification gates, so the safer assumption is that downstream actions may be taken on unverified upstream output.
conditions: IF transformers uses aci output as a source of facts or instructions without verification
IF transformers then sends email, edits CRM records, or runs browser actions based on that output
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any external action
Require transformers to cite source records for each claim
Limit aci output to structured fields with validation
Dry-run actions before committing changes
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks between agents

E_compliance.rationale: aci explicitly handles CRM, email, support, and calendar data, while transformers processes files and can egress broadly. That creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch if regulated customer data is moved into transformers workflows. No HIPAA/GDPR/DPA controls are documented for either agent, so the compliance risk is present but not fully specified.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from aci is copied into transformers-managed files or outputs
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between the two systems
mitigations: Classify data before handoff and block regulated fields
Set a short retention window for shared artifacts
Delete temporary files after each run
Confirm residency and DPA terms for any external service
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention enforcement
